title: HiRISE: High-Resolution Image Scaling for Edge ML via In-Sensor Compression and Selective ROI
problem: High-resolution images cannot be stored in memory-constrained tiny IoT devices (e.g., 512kB SRAM) without external hardware, preventing deployment of ML systems requiring high-resolution image inputs on edge devices.
motivation: Enabling practical ML inference on resource-constrained edge IoT devices for high-resolution image applications like object detection and image classification.
method: HiRISE performs analog in-sensor image scaling at the sensor level with selective region-of-interest (ROI) capability, compressing images before they are transferred to the microcontroller. Compression occurs in the analog domain at the sensor itself, eliminating the need to store large images in device memory and reducing both memory footprint and data transfer requirements.
key_novelty: Using analog in-sensor image scaling with selective ROI to compress high-resolution images at the source before transfer to memory-constrained edge devices.
contributions: HiRISE system architecture combining in-sensor analog compression with selective ROI capability
Approach to handling high-resolution images on edge devices with severely limited memory
Up to 17.7× reduction in data transfer and energy consumption
Significant reduction in peak memory requirements for edge ML deployment
limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: In-sensor analog image compression for edge ML
